title: redwood-auroracloud-marketplace-reference-arch-sync

Redwood SE to send reference architecture diagram and Terraform snippets
Schedule pilot marketplace onboarding test week of 2027-03-17
AuroraCloud to share SOC2 report access link and contact for billing integration
action_items: Diego Ruiz: Draft AMI/container packaging steps and minimal test harness; due 2027-03-17
Anika Patel: Prepare reference arch doc + IaC snippets for VPC peering, KMS integration; due 2027-03-15
Liam O'Neil: Provide AuroraCloud billing account and marketplace owner contact; due 2027-03-12
Grace Wu: Share AuroraCloud marketplace acceptance checklist and SLA onboarding window; due 2027-03-14
summary: Partner tech sync to align on Redwood listing for AuroraCloud marketplace, reference architecture for private deployment, packaging requirements, and security onboarding. Agreed on next steps: share docs, run a pilot test, exchange security artifacts, and schedule a follow-up demo for marketplace packaging.
topics: marketplace listing requirements; reference architecture (VPC, KMS, SSO); packaging (AMI vs container, Terraform modules); security/compliance (SOC2, audit logs); pilot and test plan; go-to-market listing timeline
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, i think we have about 45 minutes, i'm maya from redwood, ae on this account, uh diego and anika from our eng team are here too.
[00:08] Liam O'Neil: thanks, maya. liam from auroracloud, grace and rajiv are here on my side. excited to get the reference arch and marketplace details aligned.
[00:16] Diego Ruiz: hi all, diego (redwood se) — i'll focus on packaging and the infra bits. quick note — forgive any audio glitches, my mic is a little fuzzy.
[00:23] Sofia Martinez: sofia here, cloud eng, i'll be driving the integration work from aurora infra side.
[00:30] Maya Chen: cool. quick agenda: marketplace listing checklist, reference arch for private deployment and vpc options, packaging options (ami vs container image/helm), security artifacts, and pilot/test plan. sound good?
[00:38] Group: yep / sounds good / yep
[00:42] [00:45] Diego Ruiz: ok, so for marketplace listing — generally there are two flows we support: a pre-bundled AMI/VM image for aurora's marketplace, or a container image with helm chart for k8s marketplace. both need a listing sku, a small metadata file, and a quickstart. for aurora, do you prefer AMI-first or container-first?
[00:58] Liam O'Neil: historically we prefer container images for ease of updates, but our marketplace also supports image-ami bundles for customers who want single-click deploy. grace, thoughts?
[01:06] Grace Wu: container-first is cleaner for our cloud customers, but we do see enterprise buyers ask for an AMI option for on-prem hybrid installs. offering both is fine, but it increases our acceptance matrix.
[01:15] Anika Patel: if we do both, from redwood's side we can provide an OCI image (gcr/ecr compatible) plus an AMI build script. we'll include terraform modules for vpc peering and k8s node pool config in the reference arch.
[01:26] Rajiv Menon: security question — how are keys managed? we need to ensure we can integrate with auroracloud kms or customer-managed hsm. also audit logs and retention windows are important, and SOC2 docs.
[01:35] Diego Ruiz: yes, good point. our private deployment supports a private control plane with customer-managed KMS integration. we have two patterns: bring-your-own-kms via kms-as-a-service or use redwood-managed keys with a contractual agreement. we can emit audit logs to your S3-compatible storage or push to your SIEM via syslog/https.
[01:48] [02:00] Maya Chen: rajiv, do you have a checklist for the SOC2/ISO artifacts you need for marketplace vetting?
[02:05] Rajiv Menon: generally: SOC2 type 2 report, pen-test summary, data flow diagram, encryption at rest/in transit details, and access control policy. we also want RBAC notes — how admin vs user roles are separated.
[02:15] Anika Patel: we can share our SOC2 summary and a redacted pen-test report; i'll attach a data flow diagram and the RBAC matrix. note, some of the naming in our docs uses 'redwood dedicated' and 'redwood private' — sometimes transcription in older calls shows 'redwood privat' or 'redwood dedicate' which confused partners — ha.
[02:30] Sofia Martinez: ha, ok. for the reference arch, our customers typically want VPC peering or private link, kms integration, and the ability to pin model versions. can your runtime support pinned model rollouts and canary deploys across regions?
[02:43] Diego Ruiz: yes, our runtime supports pinning model versions and routing policies. from an infra perspective we map model variants to different node pools for isolation, and we support canary rollouts with automatic fallback to a lower-cost hosted variant if capacity spikes.
[02:58] Liam O'Neil: for marketplace listing we'll need: pricing SKU, billing integration info, acceptance tests (smoke tests), and the quickstart template. can redwood share a sample pricing matrix?
[03:08] Maya Chen: yes, we'll share a Pricing SKU template. high level: hosted api has per-token pricing, dedicated has reserved capacity commit pricing, and private has licensing + infra. for marketplace, typically customers buy a subscription or BYOL listing — we'll provide both flavors in the listing metadata.
[03:22] [03:30] Anika Patel: packaging note: for the container path we recommend an image with a small bootstrap that pulls the model artifact from a signed S3 URL or aurora artifact store. the image includes health endpoints and a test harness to run a sample inference request — that's what marketplace acceptance tests will run.
[03:42] Grace Wu: acceptance tests — we need a non-sensitive sample prompt and a deterministic output so we can validate the deploy. can you provide that?
[03:49] Diego Ruiz: yes, we'll include a smoke prompt and expected token-level structure. note: sometimes model outputs are nondeterministic so we base acceptance on structural checks (json schema, presence of keys) rather than exact text.
[04:01] Rajiv Menon: also need to confirm: audit logs location, retention policy, and who has access. this ties to our compliance team.
[04:08] Anika Patel: we'll include an audit logs doc with endpoints and sample export script. retention windows can be configured; default is 90 days on our hosted offering, but for private deployments you control retention via your storage lifecycle.
[04:20] [04:30] Maya Chen: timeline wise, if we exchange docs this week and run a short pilot the week of 3/17, we could aim for a marketplace listing submission in early April pending acceptance. does that timeline work?
[04:40] Liam O'Neil: yes that's reasonable. we usually have a 2-week review after submission.
[04:45] Sofia Martinez: do we need legal review before we submit the artifact?
[04:49] Maya Chen: it helps if billing and legal contact are included; liam, can you share your marketplace owner contact and billing team?
[04:54] Liam O'Neil: yes i'll send that after the call.
[04:58] [05:00] Diego Ruiz: technical gotchas — network egress: some customers want no egress to public internet for models; in that pattern we ship a private model artifact that sits in the customer VPC and the runtime is configured to never call home. packaging needs to support an air-gapped artifact fetch during install. that's the AMI-first pattern.
[05:15] Grace Wu: that air-gapped pattern requires extra validation on our side — we can do it but will add time to acceptance.
[05:21] Anika Patel: noted — we'll add an air-gap checklist and a small script to verify dependencies offline.
[05:28] Rajiv Menon: encryption question — TLS between services is expected, but do you support mutual TLS for inter-service comms?
[05:33] Diego Ruiz: yes mTLS is supported; we also support token-based auth injected via env or vault. we can show an example of configuring mTLS using aurora's cert manager if you want.
[05:42] [06:00] Maya Chen: ok, let's surface any blockers. liam?
[06:05] Liam O'Neil: no blockers, just need the artifacts. one ask: can redwood provide a short recorded walkthrough of the installation flow we can use internally?
[06:12] Anika Patel: yes we can record a 10-minute demo of the helm install + smoke test.
[06:17] Sofia Martinez: great. about the terraform snippets — can you include an example of the node pool sizing for low-latency workloads?
[06:23] Diego Ruiz: yes the snippet will include recommended node types, gpu counts, and batching settings. note: for latency-sensitive workloads we call out smaller batch sizes and an autoscale buffer.
[06:33] [06:45] Maya Chen: ok summarizing: redwood to send pricing SKU, marketplace checklist, reference arch + terraform and helm snippets, audit logs doc, SOC2/pen-test summaries (redacted), demo recording. aurora to share billing marketplace owner and acceptance checklist. pilot week of 3/17. next sync after pilot results.
[06:57] Grace Wu: will do.
[07:00] Rajiv Menon: i'll review the security artifacts and loop in compliance if anything looks off.
[07:06] Diego Ruiz: any competitive concerns — you mentioned aws marketplace earlier — sometimes partners ask about exclusive listings or dual-listing policies. we generally support multi-marketplace listings.
[07:17] Liam O'Neil: we support multi-listing as well, no issue.
[07:21] [07:30] Maya Chen: perfect. i'll follow up with a single email with links to the artifacts and the action-item owners. thanks everyone, appreciate the time.
[07:37] [07:45] Group: thanks / bye
[07:50] 
Notes: occasional transcription typos — e.g., 'redwood privat' in earlier docs; action items captured in meeting notes. Attached references (links to be shared): /redwood/marketplace/checklist (will be sent), /redwood/reference-arch/auroracloud/diagram-v1 (will be sent).
